sources.title: Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations
sources.locator: Contents on PDF pp. xi-xiii; §2.3 "The Open Mapping Theorem and the Closed Graph Theorem" on printed pp. 34-36, specifically Theorem 2.6, Corollaries 2.7-2.8, and Theorem 2.9; and §2.4 "Complementary Subspaces; Right and Left Invertibility of Linear Operators" on printed pp. 37-40, specifically Theorem 2.10, the definition of complementary subspaces, finite-(co)dimension examples, Remark 8, Remark 9, and Theorems 2.12-2.13.

contents.name: Theorem 2.6 (open mapping theorem)
contents.reason: FA-6 is the page that owns the full open-mapping theorem and its Baire proof. FA-2 uses quotient-ball openness only for the normed quotient, not the general Banach-space theorem.

contents.name: Corollary 2.7, a bounded bijection between Banach spaces has continuous inverse
contents.reason: FA-6 owns the standalone bounded-inverse theorem. On FA-2 the same argument is used only locally inside the bounded-below and inverse-splitting items, so the library should not mint a second independent general inverse theorem here.

contents.name: Corollary 2.8, two Banach norms comparable one way are equivalent
contents.reason: The design places this quantitative norm-equivalence corollary on FA-6 with the rest of the Baire-principle package, not on the earlier operator-and-quotient page.

contents.name: Theorem 2.9 (closed graph theorem)
contents.reason: Closed graph is one of the core FA-6 Baire consequences. Reading it here is part of the proof-route audit for later inverse and complement results, not authority to duplicate that theorem on FA-2.

contents.name: Theorem 2.10, bounded decompositions in a closed sum of closed subspaces
The definition of complementary subspaces
Finite-dimensional and finite-codimension subspaces admit complements
contents.reason: The design explicitly routes finite-dimensional complementation to FA-5, after the Hahn-Banach coordinate-extension machinery is built and available as a dependency.

contents.name: Remark 8, some closed subspaces have no complement
contents.reason: The sourced classical uncomplemented-subspace witness belongs to the later examples page that contrasts Hahn-Banach complement constructions with genuine Banach-space failures.

contents.name: Theorem 2.12, a surjective operator has a right inverse iff its kernel is complemented
Remark 9, quotient maps without right inverses from uncomplemented kernels
contents.reason: This is a companion-page obstruction example for later uncomplemented subspaces rather than a new theorem on the operator-quotient spine itself.

contents.name: Theorem 2.13, an injective operator has a left inverse iff its range is closed and complemented
